newsitem.title: CHINA: China agrees U.S. consulate in HK after handover.
newsitem.headline: China agrees U.S. consulate in HK after handover.

text.p: China and the United States are to sign an agreement on Tuesday formally allowing Washington to maintain a consulate in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Beijing rule on July 1, White House officials said.
The agreement ends months of delays as the U.S. side has awaited final word from Beijing that it would be allowed to keep a consulate in Hong Kong.
The British colony returns to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 after 150 years of British rule.
The agreement is to be signed by U.S. Ambassador to China Jim Sasser and Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Li Zhaoxing.
Visiting U.S. Vice President Al Gore will witness the ceremony in the Great Hall of the People.
